Validate Repeated Entries in Looped Questions

validate_repeated_entries.Rd

Flags looped journey questions where an entry repeats an earlier one, and writes the fix to the log: remove the repeat, move the later entries up one place and close the list with None.

Usage

validate_repeated_entries(
  dataset,
  uuid_column = "_uuid",
  sections = ck_repeated_entries_sections(),
  tool_choices = NULL,
  none_value = NULL,
  stop_values = c("996", "998", "999", "None", "Don't know", "Refused"),
  other_values = c("997", "9997", "Other", "Other country"),
  aliases = ck_country_aliases(),
  similarity = 0.85,
  sm_separator = "/",
  log_name = "repeated_entries_log",
  skip_label_row = TRUE
)

Arguments

dataset

A dataframe or a list containing a dataframe named checked_dataset.

uuid_column

Name of the uuid column. Default "_uuid".

sections

The question sets to check, in the shape returned by ck_repeated_entries_sections (the default). Pass a subset to run fewer sets, or your own list for a tool with other question names.

tool_choices

Optional. The XLSForm choices, as returned by read_tool_choices(). Used to match typed "Other" answers to the form's countries and places. Default NULL.

none_value

The value that means None, written into the freed slot when the list had no closing answer. NULL (the default) uses "None" for a labelled export and "996" for a coded one, judged from the country columns.

stop_values

Values that end the list (None, Don't know, Refused), as codes or labels. They are never treated as repeats. none_value is always included. Default c("996", "998", "999", "None", "Don't know", "Refused").

other_values

Values of the country or place question that mean "Other", as codes or labels. Default c("997", "9997", "Other", "Other country").

aliases

Other spellings of country names, see ck_country_aliases. Only used with tool_choices.

similarity

A number above 0 and up to 1. Two typed texts that are at least this similar (1 minus the edit distance over the longer length) count as a possible repeat. Default 0.85. With 1, only texts that differ in case, spacing or punctuation match.

sm_separator

The separator between a select-multiple question and its choice in the sub-column names. Default "/".

log_name

Name of the log in the returned list. Default "repeated_entries_log".

skip_label_row

Logical. If TRUE (the default), the first row of the dataset is removed before validation. ONA exports include a label/description row immediately after the header that should not be treated as survey data.

Value

A list containing:

checked_dataset

The original dataset with one logical flag column per question set (repeated_<set name>, TRUE = flagged).

<log_name>

The log, with columns uuid, old_value, question, issue and check_binding.

Details

By default three question sets are checked (see ck_repeated_entries_sections):

  • Countries transited (Q47 to Q54): the next country is the same as the one before.

  • Main stops (Q56 to Q70): the next stop has the same country and place as the one before. Same country with a different place is kept.

  • Dangerous locations (Q98 to Q117): any location with the same country and place as an earlier one, wherever it is in the loop.

For countries and stops only entries that follow each other count. Kenya, Kenya, Uganda becomes Kenya, Uganda, None; Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Kenya is left as it is. A run such as Kenya, Kenya, Kenya collapses to one Kenya.

The form only opens the next entry when the one before is not None or Refused, so blanking a repeat in the middle would leave the record breaking the form's own skip logic. Every column of the later entries is therefore moved up - the "please specify" texts, calculates and select-multiple sub-columns included. If the list ended in a closing answer (None, Refused) that answer moves up too; if every slot was filled, the freed slot gets none_value and its other columns become blank.

Blank values and stop_values are never treated as repeats. Both the codes (996) and the labels (None) of the closing answers are recognised, so the check works on coded and labelled exports.

Certain and possible repeats. A repeat is certain when the same answer is given twice in a row. Its log rows start with "Back-to-back repeat" and apply_cleaning_log() applies them whatever the reviewer filled in. A repeat is only possible when

  • the two entries are not next to each other (dangerous locations), because the removed entry's own answers, such as its risks, go with it; or

  • they only match through a typed "Other" answer: the text names the same country or place as the other entry (in any language of the form, through aliases, or with a small typo), or two typed texts are nearly the same (similarity).

Possible repeats start with "Possible repeat" and are only applied when the reviewer accepts them: set Action taken to recoded on any one row of the record and copy its suggested value into New value; apply_cleaning_log() then applies all of that record's rows. Rows left as no_action keep the answers as they are.

Typed answers are only matched to the form's choices when tool_choices is given; without it, two typed texts are still compared with each other.

The function only writes a log - the data is not changed. Each log row is one cell that has to change, and its issue says what was repeated and the suggested new value. All rows from one record and question set share a check_binding, so they get one colour on the cleaning log.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
repeated_entries_log <- cleaningkit::validate_repeated_entries(
  dataset = raw_data,
  uuid_column = "_uuid",
  tool_choices = tool_choices,
  log_name = "repeated_entries_log",
  skip_label_row = TRUE
)

# only the main stops
sets <- cleaningkit::ck_repeated_entries_sections()["main_stops"]
repeated_entries_log <- cleaningkit::validate_repeated_entries(
  dataset = raw_data,
  sections = sets
)
} # }
